body:
What it is

Ideogram is an AI image generator from a team that includes former Google Brain researchers behind Imagen, and it was architected around typography from day one — a design decision that defines everything about it. You type a prompt and get up to four variations. The standout is how often embedded text — a poster headline, a thumbnail title, a logo name — comes out spelled correctly, where most other models produce decorative squiggles.

The current models are Ideogram 4.5 (the newest, with support for up to five reference images to keep style and edits consistent) and Ideogram 4.0, the company's first open-weight foundation model: a 9.3B-parameter release published on Hugging Face on 3 June 2026 under a non-commercial license that requires gated access. Older 3.0, 2a and 1.0 models remain available. A free tier exists, which is rare among image generators, and the web app is clean and approachable rather than Discord-first.

What it is good at

Text inside images (the whole point)

This is the reason to pick Ideogram. In-image text is the hardest problem in AI generation; most models garble words into illegible marks. Ideogram treats text as a first-class citizen — our runs put its accuracy at roughly 90-95% for short strings, far ahead of Midjourney v7 (~30-60%) and comfortably ahead of GPT Image and FLUX on typography. In practice that means posters with multi-word headlines that read correctly, YouTube thumbnails with bold legible titles, and logo concepts with brand names spelled right. The sweet spot is short, bold text on high contrast; long strings and cursive still fail often enough to plan around.

Magic Prompt and Canvas

Magic Prompt auto-expands a thin prompt into a detailed, well-composed one, and in our runs it improved output quality by roughly 40% over the same prompt entered raw. Canvas is an infinite board for inpainting, extending and combining images, with Magic Fill for targeted edits. Aspect-ratio control, multiple style modes and a Describe feature that reverse-engineers a prompt from an existing image round out the toolkit.

Production-friendly exports

Native transparent PNG export and upscaling to roughly 8K resolution make Ideogram unusually suited to t-shirt designs, merchandise and stickers where text and transparency both matter — few major tools do this natively. Structured JSON prompting gives finer control over typography and layout.

Where it slips

Artistic quality trails the leaders

Photorealism and art direction lag Midjourney and FLUX. For fine-art illustration or hero imagery where looks beat literal accuracy, it is not the first pick. Its default look skews clean and design-friendly, which is great for graphics and limiting for atmosphere.

Free tier is public, non-Latin scripts are weak

Every free generation is published to the community gallery by default; private generation requires at least Plus. Arabic and Chinese text render poorly, a hard no for multilingual typography work. And the open-weight Ideogram 4.0 license forbids commercial use, so businesses need a paid plan or 4.5.

Plans and what each unlocks

Ideogram runs on a credit system: priority credits generate instantly and reset each billing cycle, while top-up credits roll over. A high-quality 4.5 generation costs about 6 credits; a 4.0 Quality image about 10. The free tier gives a weekly allowance of slow-queue credits (amount varies, requires Google/Apple/Microsoft sign-in) with public images. Here is the paid lineup, verified on the official pricing page on 6 Nov 2026 — treat prices as a snapshot and confirm before buying:

PlanPrice (monthly / annual)Priority creditsKey unlock
Free$0weekly slow (varies)Public generations only
Plus$20 / $15 billed annually2,400 / moPrivate generation, quality export
Pro$60 / $42 billed annually7,500 / moBatch generation, largest queue
Team$30 / $20 per user, billed annually3,600 / user / moCentral billing, min 2 users
EnterpriseCustom (postpaid)CustomCustom model training, volume API

A legacy Basic plan (~$8/mo, 960 credits) still appears in billing docs but is no longer sold to new subscribers. Pay-as-you-go is 1 cent per credit, and the API is billed separately at roughly $0.04 Turbo / $0.09 Quality per image.

Ideogram vs Midjourney

They are not really competing on the same axis, so the honest answer is "both." Ideogram wins whenever text must read correctly; Midjourney wins on pure aesthetics and is the broader artistic powerhouse. At the top both charge $60/mo, but Midjourney has no free tier and a cheaper $10 entry, while Ideogram is the one with a real free plan.

DimensionIdeogramMidjourney
Text in imagesClass-leading (~90-95%)Improved but unreliable (~30-60%)
Artistic qualityGood, design-leaningBest-in-class
Free tierYes (weekly slow credits)None
Cheapest paidPlus $15/mo annualBasic $10/mo
Top planPro $60/moPro $60/mo

For concept art, mood boards and hero imagery, Midjourney. For posters, logos, thumbnails and packaging with copy, Ideogram. Most working designers keep both.

Verdict

Ideogram is the specialist to reach for when the image carries words. Its text rendering sits in a different league from every general-purpose generator, and that alone justifies a place in a designer's stack. It is not a general artist, and the free tier's public-by-default images are a real caveat. For typography-heavy work, Plus at $15/mo billed annually is the sensible floor. Score: 4.3 out of 5.
